text: A linear chain of three masses: a learning bar at one end, a community commons at the other, and a civic hinge between them. The hinge gathers the school's public face (arrival, the office, the arts and the library) and acts as front door and crossroads, so every passage between learning and commons crosses it.

A compact closed cluster in which the shared realm is layered vertically: the commons volume forms the base and an arts loft rides on its roof, making one cultural block for gathering, performance and making. A civic block crowned by the library and a plain academic bar complete a triangle, each mass joined to both others.

Three free-standing pavilions on shared grounds with no built connections, read as a small campus. A self-sufficient learning pavilion also holds daily care. A community pavilion for athletics and dining can open on its own. A low civic-arts pavilion sits at arrival with the library above the office. Movement between the pavilions is outdoors.

The commons is the central heart, with a civic front on one side and a learning wing on the other, each joined only through the heart. Arrival leads into the shared volume, and the learning wing lies beyond it, buffered from public entry. The arts move into the learning wing as part of daily teaching.

A tall academy holds classrooms over the front office with the library at its crown. Beside it, a care-and-making house pairs specialized learning with the nurse and the arts. Together with the commons, the three masses close a loop around a shared court, each joined directly to the other two.

A low civic gateway stands between a three-storey learning bar and a community hall and forms the only enclosed passage between them. Everyone arrives through the gateway, where the school's front and its making and reading spaces meet visitors; classrooms extend behind it on one side and the shared hall on the other.

A shared heart gathers the school's communal life: the hall for play, dining and assembly, crowned by a studio loft for art and music. Two wings, one of classrooms and one forming the school's front with its inclusive support, attach only to the heart, so all movement between them passes through it.

One self-contained school bar carries the whole teaching day, rising from the front office and specialist support at its foot through classrooms to a reading crown. Two freestanding pavilions, a community hall and a making-and-maintenance workshop, stand apart on shared grounds and are reached outdoors.

Three ranges close around a courtyard and join at every corner into a continuous indoor loop: a tall learning range, a low civic and arts front, and a commons range whose hall is crowned by a reading loft that looks down into the court.

Classrooms stay low and close to the ground in a two-storey learning bar, flanked by the hall on one side and, on the other, a compact three-storey civic tower that stacks the school's front, its specialist support and a library crown as the building's vertical marker.

A linear sequence of three parts: a quiet learning bar at one end, an assembly hall at the other, and a compact civic hinge between them. The hinge is the front door and the school's cultural core, stacking arts and the library over the front office, so every passage between classrooms and the hall crosses the public centre of the school.

A centralized plan: the hall is the heart, and two wings plug into it from opposite sides. One wing is a complete learning house with its own arts rooms; the other is a small front-of-house wing carrying the office with the library above. The wings meet only through the heart, never directly.

A compact cluster: three three-storey masses linked to one another around a shared courtyard. The hall is not a low shed but a full-height block, crowned by an arts loft above its service side looking onto the stage. A learning bar and a civic house complete the ring, the civic house keeping specialized learning close to the office and nurse.

Two parallel learning bars joined to each other form the school proper, the library crowning the classroom bar. The hall stands apart as a freestanding community building on shared grounds. One bar is the classroom house; the other is a front and inclusion house that pairs the office with specialized learning.

One large learning block holds almost the whole school day, with the front door at its base and the library at its crown. A low, single-storey workshop pavilion for making and building service is the hinge to the hall, so hands-on work and service sit between learning and assembly.

Teaching spaces occupy a modest two-level structure that maintains a strong connection to the site. An assembly facility borders one side, while the opposite side meets a concentrated three-level public building. This taller element places reception functions below educational assistance facilities and a top-floor library, giving the composition its most prominent upward expression.

Three mutually connected buildings create a tightly arranged triangular configuration. One combines communal activities at ground level with creative studios directly overhead, accommodating social events, presentations and practical artistic work. Another contains administrative and public functions beneath an uppermost library, while a straightforward classroom structure provides the third component. Direct internal links connect every pair of buildings.

The school is arranged as three consecutive structures along a single route. Classroom accommodation occupies one extremity and communal facilities the other. Between them, a central administrative and cultural building contains reception, offices, creative teaching rooms and the library. It provides the main entrance and principal circulation junction, requiring anyone moving between the two outer buildings to pass through this middle section.

Nearly all routine educational activities take place within one substantial teaching building, which accommodates the main entrance on its lowest level and the library at its highest. An adjacent single-level structure provides practical creative workspaces and operational facilities. Positioned between the teaching building and assembly hall, this smaller element establishes their connection while concentrating fabrication activities and building services at that intermediate point.

Three buildings of equal three-level height form a closely connected arrangement surrounding an outdoor court, with direct connections between all three. The assembly facilities occupy a building of the same vertical extent as its neighbors, incorporating upper-level creative studios over the utility area with views toward the performance platform. The remaining buildings accommodate classrooms and administration, with additional educational assistance rooms adjacent to the office and health facilities.

Communal activities occupy the principal connecting structure, containing spaces for recreation, meals and schoolwide events, with visual and performing arts studios situated overhead. A classroom building and a separate entrance-and-assistance building extend from this shared facility. Neither outer building connects directly to the other, making the communal structure the necessary route for movement between instructional accommodation and administrative or inclusive services.

An assembly and activity building occupies the middle of the composition, receiving two separate extensions from opposing directions. One contains a full range of classroom facilities together with dedicated creative teaching rooms. The smaller extension houses reception and administration on its lower level and the library upstairs. No direct connection exists between these extensions; circulation from one to the other must traverse the central gathering facility.

The school operates as three distinct buildings distributed across a common site, without enclosed corridors linking them. One independently functioning teaching building includes routine student welfare provision. A second accommodates sport and meals and can operate separately for neighborhood use. The third is a shorter administration-and-creative-education building located at the entrance, placing the library over the offices. All transfers between buildings take place outside.

Three directly interconnected structures surround a common open-air space. The tallest accommodates teaching rooms on floors above the administrative entrance facilities, with the library occupying its uppermost level. A neighboring building combines additional educational assistance, healthcare and creative instruction. The communal building provides the remaining side, completing a continuous enclosed circulation arrangement in which each structure connects independently with both others.

The principal school consists of two neighboring elongated teaching buildings running alongside one another and connected directly. The first accommodates general classrooms and places the library on its highest level. The second combines reception and administrative functions with additional inclusive educational provision. A separate assembly and community facility occupies the same grounds without a built connection to either teaching building.

A short administrative and cultural building occupies the space between a three-level classroom structure and a communal assembly facility. This intermediate section provides their sole internal connection and accommodates the school's principal entrance. Reception, practical creative activities and library provision are concentrated where visitors enter, with teaching accommodation extending in one direction and the shared gathering facility in the other.

Three buildings follow a straight progression from a relatively secluded classroom structure to a communal assembly facility. Between these endpoints stands a concentrated entrance building containing administration at its lowest level and creative instruction and library accommodation above. This middle section serves as the main public arrival point and obligatory internal route between teaching areas and the assembly facility.

A communal building occupies the midpoint of the school, connecting an entrance-and-administration section on one side with classroom accommodation on the other. The two outer sections have no direct link. Visitors first enter the common activity space before reaching the teaching section beyond, separating classrooms from immediate public access. Creative subjects are incorporated into the classroom section alongside regular instruction.

The complete daily instructional program occupies a single independently functioning elongated building. Administrative reception and additional educational services occupy its lowest portion, classrooms rise above them, and the library completes the uppermost level. Elsewhere on the same property stand two physically separate structures: one for communal assemblies and another for practical creative work and upkeep operations. Access between all three requires outdoor travel.

Three connected building sections surround an open-air quadrangle, with enclosed links at each junction providing an uninterrupted circulation circuit. The classroom section rises higher than the others, while a shorter entrance section accommodates administration and creative instruction. The third section contains communal gathering facilities, with an elevated library space above the assembly area oriented toward the interior outdoor space.

A dispersed academic campus organized around a freestanding classroom block and a connected pair of shared-use volumes. Core academics and special education form a vertically layered teaching precinct, while a separate arts, media center, and support block connects directly to the recreation and dining volume. The composition establishes two distinct building clusters.

A linear three-part composition with the recreation and arts volume acting as the connecting hinge between two vertically organized learning blocks. One block combines core academics, an upper-level media center, and administration, while the other concentrates special education and support functions. The sequence forms a linked chain without a direct connection between its academic ends.

A dispersed three-pavilion campus with each mass operating as an independent architectural element. A vertically organized core academic and special education block stands apart from a recreation and dining pavilion, while a third block combines ground-level arts and administration with an elevated media center. The arrangement is defined by separation rather than internal building links.

Three detached programmatic volumes organized by distinct institutional roles. A consolidated academic building layers classrooms, special education, the media center, and support functions vertically. A separate recreation and dining pavilion includes administration, while art and music occupy an independent studio volume. The overall composition emphasizes three autonomous masses without direct connecting links.

A paired academic and student-support cluster set apart from an independent recreation and arts pavilion. The core classroom block connects directly to a vertically layered special education, administration, and media center block, forming the primary academic grouping. The detached third volume places creative learning above recreation and dining, establishing a separate stacked activity element.

A detached three-volume organization separating academic learning, recreation, and shared institutional resources. Core academics and special education occupy one consolidated teaching block, with health and maintenance functions at its base. A separate recreation and dining pavilion stands independently, as does an arts and administration block with the media center elevated above its ground-level functions.

A fully interconnected triangular campus organized around a consolidated learning block and two complementary shared-use volumes. Core academics, special education, arts, and the media center are layered within a single teaching mass. A compact administrative and support block and a recreation and dining volume complete the triangle, with direct links joining all three elements.

A tripartite detached campus with independent academic, specialized learning, and recreation volumes. The main academic building combines classrooms with administration at its base and the media center at its upper level. A second three-story block groups special education with arts and support functions, while recreation and dining occupy a separate pavilion without direct connections to either learning block.

A fully connected three-mass composition forming a triangular network between complementary educational precincts. A core academic block combines classrooms with an upper-level media center and ground-level administration. A parallel special education and arts block provides another vertically organized learning environment, while recreation and dining form the third volume, directly linking the two educational elements.

A linear sequence of three connected programmatic volumes, with an arts, media center, and support block serving as the intermediate connector. Core academics and special education form one vertically layered end, while recreation and dining occupy the opposite end. The central shared-resource element links both termini without a direct connection between them.

A fully interconnected triangular arrangement of three specialized volumes. The core academic block, a special education and student-support block, and a recreation and arts block each maintain a distinct programmatic identity. The media center crowns the student-support volume, while art and music occupy the upper level of the recreation volume. Direct links complete the three-sided network.

A linear three-part school organized around a central recreation and dining connector. One end contains a compact administration and media center block, with the media center raised above administrative functions. The opposite end consolidates core academics, special education, arts, and support programs into a layered teaching mass. The middle volume directly links the two ends.

A branching three-mass composition with recreation and dining acting as the central connector between two distinct learning blocks. One branch organizes special education, administration, and an elevated media center, while the other combines core academics with upper-level arts and ground-level maintenance. The two learning branches remain unlinked to each other, producing a hinged configuration.

A fully interconnected triangular school composed of three complementary vertical program blocks. Core academics, administration, and the media center form one learning volume, while special education is stacked over a recreation and dining base in another. A third compact block houses arts, health, and maintenance functions. Direct connections between every pair create a closed three-part network.

A two-part connected cluster accompanied by a freestanding core academic building. The connected pair joins a vertically layered special education, administration, and media center block to a recreation volume crowned by art and music. The separate classroom block retains its own three-story academic identity, establishing a primary linked activity cluster alongside an independent teaching mass.

A detached main teaching block paired with a connected shared-resource and recreation cluster. Core academics and special education are vertically consolidated with administration at the base, forming an independent educational mass. The second cluster joins a layered arts and media center block to the recreation and dining volume, establishing a two-part support and activity grouping apart from classrooms.

A linear three-volume arrangement with recreation and dining forming the intermediate link between two separate learning blocks. Core academics rise toward an upper-level media center above ground-level administration at one end. At the other, special education occupies a three-story block alongside arts and support functions. The middle pavilion connects both ends without a direct academic-to-academic link.

A linked three-part sequence organized around a central recreation and dining volume. At one end, a compact institutional block stacks the media center above administration, medical, and maintenance functions. At the other, a consolidated teaching block contains core academics, special education, and ground-level arts. The central activity volume connects the two otherwise separate blocks.

A fully connected triangular composition organized around three differentiated program zones. One combines special education and administration with a recreation and dining base; another consolidates core academics with ground-level arts; and the third concentrates the media center above medical and maintenance functions. Direct links between all three establish an interconnected network of learning, activity, and shared resources.

A paired academic and recreation cluster accompanied by a detached student-support building. The core academic block places the media center at its upper level and connects directly to a recreation volume with art and music elevated above it. A separate two-story special education block combines medical and administrative functions, remaining physically independent of the connected academic and activity pair.

A linear three-part school with a special education and support block operating as the connecting hinge. A consolidated academic and arts volume stacks classrooms, creative spaces, and an upper-level media center at one end. Recreation and dining occupy the other end, connected through the intermediate special education, administration, and medical block rather than directly to the academic volume.

A branching configuration centered on a consolidated academic and creative-learning building. Core academics, special education, and ground-level arts form the primary vertical teaching mass. Two distinct connected branches extend from it: an administrative, medical, and maintenance block, and a recreation volume supporting an elevated media center. The two branches remain disconnected from each other.

A branched three-mass composition with the core academic building acting as the central connector. Its three-story classroom structure and ground-level support functions link directly to a dedicated recreation and dining pavilion and to a specialized learning block. The latter combines special education, arts, administration, and an elevated media center, while the two attached branches remain mutually unconnected.

A linear three-part arrangement with a recreation and arts volume as the central hinge. The main classroom block connects to one side, while a special education, administration, and media center block connects to the other. Creative learning is elevated above the recreation base, and the two academic blocks remain separate except through their shared intermediate volume.

A detached main academic building accompanied by a linked special education and activity cluster. Core classrooms occupy a vertically organized block with ground-level administration and an upper-level media center. Separately, the special education and arts block connects directly to the recreation, dining, and medical volume. The composition establishes an independent primary academic element beside a connected secondary grouping.

A fully interconnected triangular arrangement with a compact shared-resource block mediating between teaching and activity volumes. The academic mass consolidates core classrooms, special education, and arts, while the resource mass places the media center above ground-level administration, medical, and maintenance functions. Recreation and dining complete the triangle, with each volume directly linked to the other two.

A linear three-part configuration with the recreation and dining volume forming the central connector. A vertically consolidated core academic and special education block anchors one end, while an arts and institutional support block with an elevated media center anchors the other. Both terminal blocks connect to the middle activity volume but have no direct link to one another.

A two-volume academic and shared-resource cluster set apart from an independent recreation and administration pavilion. The main teaching block vertically combines core academics, special education, and arts. It connects directly to a support volume crowned by the media center, with medical and maintenance functions below. The recreation volume remains detached, carrying administration alongside its ground-level activity programs.

A dispersed three-pavilion composition with no direct links between its constituent masses. One vertically layered teaching volume combines core academics, special education, and medical functions. A second pavilion contains recreation and dining, while a third concentrates arts, administration, and maintenance beneath an elevated media center. The organization maintains three separate programmatic identities across the site.

A detached consolidated teaching block and a connected shared-resource and activity pair. The teaching volume vertically integrates core academics and special education with ground-level arts, medical, and maintenance functions. Separately, a compact administration and media center block connects to recreation and dining, establishing a two-mass institutional cluster independent of the principal classroom building.

A detached core learning block accompanied by a connected arts, support, and recreation cluster. Core academics and special education are vertically consolidated beneath an upper-level media center in one independent mass. A separate arts and support block connects directly to the recreation and dining volume, creating a linked activity grouping with no direct building connection to the academic mass.

A linear three-volume school organized around an intermediate arts and shared-resource block. The core academic and special education mass forms one end of the sequence, while recreation and dining form the other. Between them, creative learning, administration, medical functions, and an upper-level media center occupy the connecting volume, linking the two termini without a direct connection.

A fully interconnected triangular composition of academic, shared-activity, and creative-support volumes. The primary academic mass combines core classrooms and special education across three levels, with the media center at the top. A recreation and dining volume incorporates administration, while a separate ground-level arts, medical, and maintenance block completes the network. All three masses are directly linked.

A central recreation and administration volume connected to the main teaching block, with a detached arts and media center pavilion. Core academics and special education occupy a vertically consolidated classroom mass, linked directly to recreation, dining, medical, and administrative functions. The independent creative-learning pavilion places the media center above art and music, forming a separate third element.

A fully interconnected triangular arrangement combining three distinctly layered program volumes. The main teaching mass consolidates core academics and special education, while a compact administrative and health block places the media center above its ground-level functions. The recreation and dining volume supports an upper-level arts component. Direct connections among all three establish a closed spatial network.
